boredom-activity-detection-mechanism.modifications: Enforces isBoredom and initiatedBy when boredom markers present

activity-state-transformation-tracking.modifications: Adds state capture calls at lifecycle points

sharedComponents.analysis: Different concerns - marker enforcement is orthogonal to state tracking. Marker enforcement modifies activity metadata, state tracking observes activity lifecycle. No overlap in logic or data.
sharedComponents.recommendation: No action required - specifications are compatible

boredom-activity-detection-mechanism.usage: Idle detection, activity execution, runtime state

sharedComponents.analysis: Exclusive to boredom specification. No other specification touches this component.

impulse-usage-tracking.modifications: Records impulse IDs in activity execution metadata

sharedComponents.analysis: All specifications use impulse data read-only for different purposes. No overlapping writes or contradictory requirements. Usage is complementary: tracking records usage, state capture snapshots state, sidebar displays to user.
sharedComponents.recommendation: No action required - read-only usage patterns are compatible

boredom-activity-detection-mechanism.usage: Caller - invokes executeActivityInline for boredom activities

activity-state-transformation-tracking.usage: Instrumentor - adds state capture calls inside executeActivityInline

sharedComponents.analysis: Instrumentation is transparent to callers. BoredomManager calls executeActivityInline as normal, state tracking captures state during execution. No API changes or behavioral modifications visible to callers.
sharedComponents.recommendation: No action required - instrumentation is non-breaking

integrationPoints.name: Activity Execution
integrationPoints.description: Boredom detection creates activities with isBoredom=true and initiatedBy metadata. State tracking captures state for ALL activities, including boredom-triggered ones.
integrationPoints.analysis: State tracking is transparent and works for all activities regardless of origin (user-initiated or boredom-triggered). Boredom markers (isBoredom, initiatedBy) are captured as part of activity state. No special handling required.
benefits: Boredom activities are automatically included in learning data
State tracking provides visibility into boredom activity execution
No integration work required - works out of the box

integrationPoints.name: Impulse Usage Metrics
integrationPoints.description: Impulse tracking records impulses_loaded and impulses_created arrays in activity execution metadata. State tracking includes impulse_ids in state snapshots.
integrationPoints.analysis: Both track impulses independently for different purposes. Impulse tracking provides learning metrics (load frequency, token consumption). State tracking provides point-in-time snapshots (which impulses were loaded at state capture time). No overlap or conflict.
benefits: Complementary data: tracking provides longitudinal data, state provides snapshots
Different use cases: tracking for learning, state for debugging/analysis

integrationPoints.name: UI Data Pipeline
integrationPoints.description: Sidebar displays impulse state to users. Impulse tracking provides data for impulse metrics that can be consumed by UI.
integrationPoints.analysis: Sidebar is a consumer of impulse data. Impulse tracking provides richer metrics (load count, token consumption, cost attribution) that sidebar can display. One-way dependency: sidebar depends on tracking, but tracking is independent of sidebar.
benefits: Sidebar can display advanced impulse metrics from tracking system
Tracking provides data foundation for future UI features
Clean separation: tracking owns data, sidebar owns display

specifications.name: boredom-activity-detection-mechanism
specifications.analysis: No dependencies on other specifications. Operates independently. Other specifications do not depend on boredom detection.

specifications.name: impulse-usage-tracking
specifications.analysis: No dependencies on other specifications. Provides data that sidebar can consume. Sidebar dependency is optional (sidebar works without tracking, just with less data).

specifications.name: activity-state-transformation-tracking
specifications.analysis: No dependencies on other specifications. Transparent instrumentation that works for all activities. No other specifications depend on state tracking.

specifications.name: sidebar-impulse-visibility
specifications.analysis: Can optionally consume data from impulse-usage-tracking for richer metrics. Works independently without tracking (displays basic impulse state). No other specifications depend on sidebar.

dependencyAnalysis.analysis: All dependencies are one-way and optional. No circular dependencies. Clean separation of concerns. Each specification can be deployed independently without breaking others.

crossComponentAnalysis.method: Manual analysis based on validation results and trace documents
crossComponentAnalysis.recommendation: No CPG analysis required - manual analysis sufficient for current specifications

checks.details: Shared components have non-overlapping concerns (markers, state tracking, read-only usage)
All data flows are compatible and complementary

systemConsistency.overallAssessment: System is internally consistent. All specifications work together to provide complementary functionality without conflicts.

recommendations.recommendation: No action required - all specifications are compatible
recommendations.rationale: Conflict analysis shows 0 conflicts across 4 specifications and 4 shared components. All integration points are compatible. System is internally consistent.

recommendations.recommendation: Consider enhancing sidebar with impulse tracking metrics
recommendations.rationale: Sidebar-impulse-visibility can optionally consume data from impulse-usage-tracking to display richer metrics (load frequency, token consumption, cost attribution). This is a future enhancement, not a requirement.

recommendations.recommendation: Boredom activities are automatically included in learning data
recommendations.rationale: State tracking captures all activities, including boredom-triggered ones. No special handling required. Learning system will automatically learn from boredom activity execution patterns.

conclusion: No conflicts detected. All 4 specifications (boredom-activity-detection-mechanism, impulse-usage-tracking, activity-state-transformation-tracking, sidebar-impulse-visibility) are compatible and can coexist. Specifications work together to provide complementary functionality: boredom detection creates special activities with markers, state tracking captures all activity execution, impulse tracking provides metrics, sidebar displays state to users. System is internally consistent with clean separation of concerns and no circular dependencies.
